llm.summary: October payrolls detonated the dovish trade: +165K versus a ~65K consensus with unemployment slipping to 4.1%, and traders are now pricing a December Fed *hike* rather than a cut. That resolves yesterday's binary in the hawkish direction — 10Y yields up, dollar firmer, gold off ~1% toward $4,050 (still set for its biggest weekly gain since August), and the three-week mortgage-rate rally at 7.18% is immediately at risk. The AI complex, which just had the second-worst day on record for chip stocks, is bouncing rather than breaking: AMD +8%, NVDA/INTC +5%, AMAT gapping +8.6%, CRWV +8.5%, TSMC +7% as Taiwan restricted short selling and Beijing's State Council openly jawboned its market higher. Yesterday's violent independent-power wipeout is already half-reversing with VST gapping +6.5% into earnings, which argues the data-center-power political panic was a one-day overshoot rather than a new regime. Brent is down 13.1% on the week on weak Chinese demand — a clean margin gift to DAL and FDX and a genuine disinflationary offset to the wage story. HUM gapped +4.8% on a raised profit outlook with revenue +26%, a direct positive read-through for CI, and ABNB gapped +9.6% on raised guidance, confirming the travel/experiences trade DAL rides. The regime print is the real story: Stagflation 34.0 (+15.2 trend) and Reflation 31.7 (+10.4) rising together while Goldilocks collapses to 16.5, with rotation scores of Health Care 96, Staples 94, Real Estate 86, Materials 85, Financials 83 against Technology -81 and Comm Services -56. The book's insurance/healthcare/defensive-value tilt is sitting exactly where capital is going; the live risks are MAS (rates), BBY (memory-driven device inflation into holiday) and a short-cover squeeze in mega-cap tech muting relative performance.

market_thesis.short_term: Two opposing forces. The hawkish repricing from a 165K payroll print hits everything duration-sensitive — gold, housing/mortgage names, long bonds, and the 'rate relief' bid under Real Estate and homebuilding suppliers. Simultaneously the AI unwind is being bought: dip-buyers, Taiwan's short-selling restriction, and Beijing's explicit stabilisation call are mechanical supports that can produce a sharp, low-quality squeeze in semis and neoclouds for a few sessions. Expect index-level chop with Value holding its ~130-point lead but no longer widening. market_thesis.medium_term: Stagflation at 34.0 with a +15.2 trend and Goldilocks collapsing to 16.5 is the defining signal for the next several months: a labour market strong enough to prevent easing, prices sticky enough that the BoE already hiked to 4% and warns of ~5% inflation, and a Fed whose own speakers (Hammack, Barkin) are openly discussing a gradual hike path. That caps multiple expansion for long-duration growth and keeps the rotation into Health Care, Staples, Materials and Financials intact. Within AI, the bifurcation sharpens: contracted physical layers (semicap — AMAT's +8.6% gap, foundry, memory) keep compounding while the financing layer gets repriced — Nvidia's $108.5B of guarantees against six-year asset lives at neoclouds, IREN's $4B of annualised revenue delayed at customer request, and Goldman/Apollo syndicating slices of SpaceX's $40B Nvidia chip lease are all signs the marginal AI dollar is now credit, not cash flow. Memory scarcity shows up as a visible consumer price event in phones and PCs through 1H27, which is a volume risk for BBY even as ticket rises. Chinese demand weakness (oil down, carbon emissions -3.1%) is a global disinflationary counterweight that keeps energy rotation fading (56, down from 88).
market_thesis.long_term: The structural trade remains: the constraint on AI is power, permits, land and local political consent — hence Meta funding seven gas plants for a single data centre and Nvidia retrofitting Apollo's old phone buildings. That favours regulated utilities, gas, nuclear, copper and grid hardware over fabless storytelling, but only after the market finishes deciding who captures versus who is taxed on those electrons; yesterday's IPP crash and today's partial reversal is that argument in real time. Supply chains keep duplicating under tariffs and export controls (China probing EU chemicals, Canada-US tariff drag, Moonshot routing to European neoclouds for GPUs), embedding a permanently higher capex baseline and a higher inflation floor. On the household side, the wealthiest decile pulling further ahead while record numbers of first-time buyers pay all-cash entrenches a decade of bifurcation: value retail, generics and distribution, insurance, healthcare delivery and experiences take share from undifferentiated discretionary. Reshoring attention up 74% versus its 28-day baseline says the public is only now internalising a capex cycle that has already been running for three years.
